    {
     "subtitle": "Reporting from England: Between the magic of Old Trafford and the bitterness of the Poljud defeat",
     "screenshot_description": "Hosts Profa and Denis report from a hotel room in England after watching the derby and the match at Old Trafford.",
     "content": "Podcast hosts **Profa** and **Denis** report from England, explaining to viewers why this time they were neither at Poljud nor in their usual studio. Denis reveals how they got a unique opportunity to be guests of the former Dinamo coach, attend a training session, and watch the match between Hull and Everton. Before heading to the iconic Old Trafford to watch the clash between **Manchester United** and **Tottenham** live, they watched the biggest Croatian derby between **Hajduk** and **Dinamo** in their hotel room.\n\nProfa vividly compares going to the 'Theatre of Dreams' after a painful defeat in Split to the well-known saying that 'it is better to cry in a Porsche'. Denis admits that the match between United and Tottenham itself was not top-notch until the red card and goals in the second half, but points out that he was completely thrilled by the overall ambiance of English football, which they have been following since childhood. Before moving on to the painful topic of the Poljud derby, Profa takes the opportunity to send sporting greetings and sincere congratulations to his friends **Tonči** and **Luka** on their team's victory.",

    {
     "subtitle": "Bamba's dominance and energy crisis: 'Hajduk outplayed and beat up Dinamo'",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis energetically explains how he would frame a picture of Bamba in Dinamo's locker room after the defeat.",
     "content": "Opening the analysis of the derby, Profa draws a parallel with **Kobe Bryant's** famous interview after losing the finals to Detroit, when the basketball legend stated that he could find a hundred alibis, but would not take a single one. Although Dinamo could look for excuses in the absence of **Josip Mišić**, an insufficiently recovered **Luka Stojković**, a bad pitch, or a potential red card for the hosts, the hosts agree that there is no room for alibis, especially since in the last nine serious matches Dinamo has recorded a worrying record of three wins, three draws, and three losses.\n\nDenis is extremely sharp and resolute in his assessment: **Hajduk** was better and completely deservedly won. He points out that the problem lies in the poor game setup and a very problematic starting lineup for Dinamo. \n\n> \"If I were the coach or director of Dinamo, I would print out these eleven Hajduk players on the nicest printer and put it in the locker room. I would say: they didn't just beat you, they beat you up and outplayed you. And I would frame Bamba's picture and put it in front of the entire Dinamo defense and say: this guy dominated you!\"\n\nDenis considers it particularly devastating that at certain moments Dinamo stood in a low or mid block against a team against which, on paper, they have at least ten better players in the starting eleven. Using a metaphor about a married couple of good people between whom love and energy have simply disappeared, Denis concludes that the current coaching staff and playing squad are no longer compatible with Dinamo's expectations and that the team urgently needs shock therapy. He adds that coach **Kovačević**, with his substitutions in the 60th minute, actually admitted himself that he had missed the mark with everything he had envisioned in preparing for the match.",

     "subtitle": "The Stojković case and worrying European stumbles",
     "screenshot_description": "The hosts discuss the downward trend of Dinamo's form and poor performances in European matches.",
     "content": "Discussing the status of **Stojković**, Denis does not blame the coach for not including him in the starting eleven if the information from the press conference that the player only started training on Friday is correct. Moreover, he believes that on such a soft and muddy pitch he should not have been brought into the game at all, just as there was not much logic in bringing him in during the earlier match against **Vukovar**.\n\nWhat worries much more is the fact that Dinamo's game currently resembles nothing, and a crucial European match against **Anderlecht** is just around the corner. Denis warns that Kovačević has failed every exam where a breakthrough in results was needed. Although Profa notes that the coach can justifiably hide behind the club's official communication that simply entering the Europa League was the primary goal, both agree that the draw offered an open path to the Champions League and that the trend of form is in a steep decline.\n\n- Against modest **Thun**, Dinamo went through exclusively on luck and thanks to a red card, without being the better opponent over two matches.\n- Matches against **Viking**, **Celta**, and **Lille** showed serious limits.\n- Denis calls the performance against **Hapoel** on neutral ground the most shameful match and the most devastating game idea in Kovačević's entire mandate.\n\nProfa adds that the coach can 'light a candle at Kamenita vrata' because the international break, along with all the fuss around the stadium, at least temporarily masked the heavy slaps received from **Osijek** and Hapoel and the struggle with **Lokomotiva**.",

     "subtitle": "Criticism of Zvonimir Boban's transfer window and the unfair sidelining of Galešić",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis sharply criticizes the club's sports policy, the poorly executed transfer window, and the treatment of individual players.",
     "content": "Analyzing the deeper causes of the bad atmosphere, Denis points out that in football and in life, unfair moves always come back to haunt you. As the most vivid example, he cites the status of **Galešić**, a guy who is perhaps Dinamo's best defensive player this season, and who inexplicably does not participate in the starting lineup alongside the insecure **Dominguez**. In addition, the club has wronged a number of other players, including **Kačavenda** and **Fran Topić**, who was incredibly written off overnight.\n\nDenis delivers a very sharp criticism of **Zvonimir Boban**, pointing out that a person with such decision-making power, contacts, and resources should not have allowed himself such a catastrophic transfer window:\n\n- Bringing in completely unfit players in crucial positions.\n- Failing to bring in an adequate goalkeeper.\n- Entering a sort of 'crazy masochism' and exhausting battles over the stadium issue.\n\nAll this created a huge tangle of negative energy around the management and the coach. Denis explains how last year Kovačević had the firm and stable figure of Zvonimir Boban behind him, which gave him maximum authority. Today, when that backing is no longer held so firmly, the coach can no longer find his way in it, and the players – as 'the most perishable goods in the world' – immediately feel such weakness and loss of authority.",

    {
     "subtitle": "Tactical helplessness without Josip Mišić and analysis of Hajduk's first goal",
     "screenshot_description": "A conversation about the importance of European competitions for the club's budget and tactical mistakes in the midfield.",
     "content": "To Profa's question of whether one should worry about the championship title, Denis answers with a counter-question about worrying for Europe, which is the main pillar of the club's long-term financial stability. Without successful play in the **Europa League**, there is neither a showcase for selling players nor a filling of the budget, especially in a situation where the bridge to their own youth academy has been burned, and young players are not getting a chance at all.\n\nLooking back at the first goal conceded at Poljud, the hosts absolve center-back **McKenna** of blame, stating that he was only the third in line and that from his angle he did not see the ball at all. Denis praises the tactical preparation of Hajduk's coach **Garcia** on set pieces, while Profa highlights the excellent ball by **Šimun Hrgović**. However, the root of the problem lies in the absence of **Josip Mišić**.\n\nDenis believes that it is 'football suicide' to insist on the same postulates and the 4-3-3 formation in extraordinary circumstances when two key creators, Mišić and Stojković, are missing at Poljud. Profa notices how Dinamo's adaptation boiled down to completely skipping the midfield with long balls from the back line. Instead of creating a new tactical model or changing the formation to 4-2-3-1, an attempt was made to make a poor copy of Mišić. Denis concludes that Dinamo has become so predictable that even amateurs with scant knowledge could easily scout them, which is why Garcia took a complete tactical victory without major problems.",

     "subtitle": "The chronic right-back problem, credit for Dominguez, and lack of self-criticism",
     "screenshot_description": "The hosts analyze the problematic right-back position and strange criteria in selecting the center-back pairing.",
     "content": "A special part of the analysis is dedicated to the right-back position and defensive solutions. Profa points out that Bamba actually did all the damage on the other side, but he is bothered by the defensive stance of coach Kovačević, who is amazed by journalists' questions about the lineup, while at the same time publicly 'throwing **Valinčić** under the bus' with statements that he is in a crisis.\n\nDenis openly says that the existing choice at right-back simply does not have the quality for big Dinamo matches, nor does he have any resale potential because at 23 years old he is no longer a young player. He believes that Dinamo should shut down its youth academy if it cannot produce a better full-back, and adds that forcing such solutions ahead of the proven **Galešić** shows that the decision was either imposed from the top or the coach is completely lost.\n\nEqually unclear is the unlimited credit that center-back **Dominguez** enjoys with the coach:\n- At the center-back positions, Dinamo has the greatest depth, including Galešić and **Radeljić**.\n- Dominguez has already made over ten direct mistakes in important matches at a high level, including the foul from which Hajduk's equalizing goal came.\n\nBoth hosts are extremely frustrated by the chronic lack of self-criticism from coach Kovačević after defeats. Denis points out that his statements seem as if he is 'leading Boy Scouts on a weekend trip', and Profa adds that he literally predicted that the coach would once again reach for the platitude that 'he cannot fault his players for anything'.",

    {
     "subtitle": "Why Dinamo forces 4-3-3 and who actually outplayed the Blues?",
     "screenshot_description": "Profa and Denis discuss the ineffectiveness of Dinamo's wingers and the pointlessness of forcing the 4-3-3 system.",
     "content": "After reading a message from viewer **Ana Lovrić**, who praised Hajduk's braver approach, the hosts confirm that the Split team came out much more determined in the second half, won all the 'second balls', and was significantly better positioned in the midfield. Profa emphasizes that he would have accepted the defeat more easily if **Marko Livaja** had scored two masterful goals, but the fact that they were outplayed and beaten up by this kind of Hajduk lineup – which recently suffered at Rujevica – requires a sharp reaction towards Dinamo's players.\n\nShifting the focus to Dinamo's attack, Profa asks a crucial question: what were Dinamo's wingers doing in the derby, given that the 4-3-3 system was created precisely to maximize their output? Denis answers briefly – nothing. He criticizes the basic tactical lack of grounding of the players, wrong entries into corridors, and misguided choices of positions, stating that he would definitely have started with **Hoxha** on the left wing, and **Topić** on the right.\n\nIn the analysis of individual performance, two extremes stand out:\n- **Miha Zajc** experienced an inexplicable and drastic drop in form, although last season alongside Stojković he was the best player in the league.\n- **Dion Drena Beljo** remains the only bright spot and positive surprise because he continuously scores over 20 goals per season, which has been a rarity in the HNL since the time of **Duje Čop**.\n\nIn conclusion, Denis questions the very logic of unconditionally forcing the 4-3-3 formation. He states that in conversations with numerous coaches over the last five months, he has not heard a single coherent argument for why Dinamo must play exclusively in that system. While such unification of the system from juniors to seniors makes sense for developmental clubs where the result is not primary, for Dinamo – which must win trophies and play in Europe to fill a huge budget – such rigidity makes no sense at all. In addition, the hosts reject the rain and 'water polo conditions' as an alibi, reminding that Dinamo created its only chances precisely when the pitch became irregular.",

     "subtitle": "Coach Kovačević's tied hands: A story heading towards its end",
     "screenshot_description": "A conversation about Kovačević's coaching status, the exhaustion of relationships, and comparisons with great European coaches.",
     "content": "Analyzing the position of coach **Kovačević**, the hosts try to maintain objectivity. Profa rejects superficial comments from those who have claimed since day one that 'Kova is not a coach for Dinamo', reminding that last season he achieved the set goals and that he continuously worked more matches on the Blues' bench than most of his predecessors. \n\nDenis draws a parallel with top world coaches like **Pep Guardiola** at Manchester City or **Jürgen Klopp** in his last season at Borussia Dortmund. Such examples prove that football is not exact mathematics; sometimes processes simply come to their end, circumstances change, and the initial energy is irretrievably lost.\n\n> \"What bothers me the most in all of this is that Kovačević never actually got a chance at Dinamo all the way. We could never see what his real coaching potential was because his hands were tied the whole time in terms of creation.\"\n\nDenis reminds how Kovačević, while managing **Slaven Belupo**, often and successfully changed formations during the matches themselves, while at Dinamo a strict tactical framework was imposed on him. Although it is understandable why he accepted the opportunity of a lifetime under such conditions, today it is questionable how to reverse the negative trend at all. Referring to the coach's vague statements about being late with substitutions in Split, Denis repeats that players coming off the bench a couple of minutes earlier would not have changed anything significantly because the match was lost already in the preparation itself and the selection of the starting eleven.",

     "subtitle": "Comment on Igor Pajač's refereeing: Why referees must not be an alibi for Dinamo fans?",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis criticizes Igor Pajač's refereeing style, as well as Dinamo fans who look to the referee as the reason for the defeat.",
     "content": "In the final part of the analysis of the Poljud derby, the hosts touch upon the refereeing of **Igor Pajač**. Denis points out that the criteria were not good on either side and that Hajduk would have justifiably 'breathed fire' had they not won, since **Kačavenda** and **Dominguez** did not receive clear yellow cards for harsh fouls and unsportsmanlike conduct in the early phase of the match. He especially criticizes Pajač's style of managing the match and losing authority through endless conversations:\n\n- Instead of clearly punishing with cards, the referee allowed overly harsh play.\n- Every foul was followed by a minute-and-a-half 'interview' with the players and unnecessary explanations.\n\nRegarding the controversial tackle on the Dinamo player, both Denis and Profa – although they watched the match on their mobile phones – agree that this reckless foul on such a difficult pitch should have been sanctioned with a direct red card. Profa admits that at that moment he thought the scenario from the match against Thun would be repeated, where Dinamo with a player more would undeservedly pull through despite poor play.\n\nDespite refereeing mistakes and statistics according to which in eight derbies refereed by Pajač Dinamo has not a single victory (five Hajduk wins and three draws), Denis is appalled by the fact that Dinamo fans on social media are putting the focus on the refereeing. He concludes that the referee is only tenth on the list of problems and that with so many objective tactical and personnel blunders by their own team, Dinamo fans have no right whatsoever to whine and look for alibis in the refereeing.",

     "content": "The hosts used a break from heavy football analyses after the derby to recount impressions from their trip to England. Denis encouraged Profa to show the viewers the souvenir he bought without any haggling. Laughing, Profa revealed that he bought as many as three scarves featuring **Cristiano Ronaldo**.\n\nHe also shared an anecdote from a visit to the National Football Museum, where at the beginning he was quite disappointed and angry due to the poor representation of the Portuguese star. However, his mood improved drastically upon arriving in front of **Old Trafford**. There, while he was still staggering under the impression of Dinamo's defeat, he was greeted by a photograph showing two of his biggest football favorites in the same place.\n\nIt was the legendary photograph of Ronaldo's free kick and goal against **Portsmouth**, while **Niko Kranjčar** was in the wall, right in the path of the ball. That sight completely calmed Profa down, who in the end, after a brief discussion with a vendor about sold-out items, still managed to find a stall and equip himself with Ronaldo memorabilia.",

     "content": "Answering questions and donations from viewers, which included jokes about the expensive life in England where for 20 pounds, as Denis says, you only get a 'good day', the hosts addressed a crucial question: what is the main reason why **Dinamo** is playing worse than last season?\n\nProfa detected several connected factors as the main reasons:\n- **Saturation with the coach**, which seems to him to be the first and most obvious problem in the team\n- **A poorly executed transfer window**\n- **Psychological disappointment** after being knocked out in earlier European matches\n\nDenis followed up by pointing out that the overall energy in the club has changed. In his opinion, the pressure and insecurity from the top of the management spilled over onto the coach's back, which the players in the locker room felt very quickly and became shaken. He particularly emphasized that it is not clear to him why the public persistently avoids openly saying that Dinamo had one of the worst transfer windows and that the current team is simply noticeably weaker. Nevertheless, as a rare bright spot from the derby, he praised the attitude of the young player who came off the bench for the last fifteen minutes.",

     "subtitle": "Comment on English food, foreign referees in the HNL, and foreigners in defense",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis heatedly explains why he opposes bringing foreign referees into the Croatian league.",
     "content": "A brief intermezzo about English gastronomy provoked a fierce reaction from Denis. He concluded that there is nothing worse than English food, appalled by the fact that beans are served for breakfast, and along the way he also criticized the appearance of local women.\n\nThe conversation quickly returned to domestic football topics through a viewer's question about hiring foreign referees. While Profa would immediately appoint them in matches against **Hajduk** due to constant complaints from the Split camp, Denis expressed a diametrically opposite view. He would ban foreign referees by decree in the **HNS** and insist exclusively on domestic ones. He believes that domestic referees will never progress nor reach the big stage if they do not referee the biggest derbies, adding that Croatia is not a wild environment like Greece or Turkey that it could not create a normal working environment for referees.\n\nTo a persistent question from a viewer about how Dinamo's defense, composed of players of completely different nationalities without domestic players, can function, the hosts agreed that this is not the real cause of the problem. Profa reminded that Hajduk also had six foreigners in the starting eleven in the derby, while Denis emphasized that in world football there are numerous examples where players of different nationalities function flawlessly. He concluded that **Kovačević** proved last season that he can lead such a group, but in the meantime relationships have been lost and the story between the coach and Dinamo is simply worn out.",

     "content": "Analyzing the statistics of this season's away games, the hosts arrived at the devastating data about the lack of away wins in important matches. Listing matches against **Istra**, **Osijek**, **Hajduk**, and European clashes, Denis emphasized that those European teams against which Dinamo lost points are all weaker teams than the Zagreb club.\n\nThis was followed by the reading of provocative comments from Hajduk fans, to which Profa retorted with a reminder of Dinamo's multi-year dominance and the hundreds of days it took the people from Split to get a victory, while Denis interrupted him laughing, saying he cannot take him seriously in an angry discussion while he is wearing as many as three **Cristiano Ronaldo** scarves around his neck. They also briefly referred to viewers' messages about the alleged throwing of flares in the stadium, but Denis refused to comment on it because they neither saw nor heard the situation.\n\nThe atmosphere was further relaxed by a question from the chat directed at Denis about how he can be a guest on podcasts that have fewer than ten thousand subscribers. Denis jokingly played along, saying that big podcasts do not call him so he has to visit 'small boutiques', and invited viewers to follow **Podcast 8_24** so that they too might reach that number one day.      "content": "To a viewer's question about what they would do with coach **Kovačević** at this moment, Profa admitted that in earlier conversations he had stated that no one would be able to defend the coach anymore in the event of a defeat at Poljud. Nevertheless, since instant shock therapy does not necessarily guarantee success, he believes that Kovačević should remain on the bench for the upcoming European match against **Anderlecht**, and that this should be his absolute final exam.\n\nA question from the chat prompted Denis to tell an interesting story about his first football steps in Dinamo's open school. He recalled how as a boy of six and a half at his grandmother's house, who regularly bought **Večernji list**, he spotted an ad for enrollment in **Dinamo**. Having just learned to read, he tore out the ad and ran with the newspaper so they would enroll him.\n\nHe passed the first selection in the '91 generation, in which the most famous name was **Kramarić**, who also made the biggest career out of that team. With great respect, Denis recalled his first coach at Dinamo, **Vlado Novak**, describing him as a top-notch man and an excellent pedagogue for working with children, and he also mentioned **Davor Blašković**, the son of a former player from the famous 1967 generation, who was also his coach.",

     "subtitle": "Impressions of England, the high cost of living, and announcement of going to the Hull match",
     "screenshot_description": "Profa explains how he got tickets for the Manchester United and Tottenham derby the day before the match.",
     "content": "In the final part of the conversation, the hosts summarized their impressions of England outside the football stadiums. Profa pointed out that he really likes the local brick architecture and the relaxed nature of the people, while citing the bad weather and the appearance of the women as his main complaints, joking that it is now completely clear to him why **Cristiano Ronaldo** once went to **Madrid**. Denis, on the other hand, was unpleasantly surprised by the large number of homeless people on the streets.\n\nThey also touched upon the extreme high cost of living in England. Denis estimated that for basic survival during the day, including public transport, train, or taxi, significantly more than 50 pounds is needed. Nevertheless, Profa expressed pleasant surprise at the price and availability of tickets for the **Manchester United** and **Tottenham** match. He managed to buy a ticket just the day before the match at a price of 80 pounds, with mandatory club membership, which he considers very affordable given the reputation of the stadium and the opponent.\n\nFor the next day, they announced the continuation of their adventure and going to the **Hull** and **Everton** match, where they are guests at the invitation of their former coach.
